column2: How do I fill in the coordinates of my places from Google Earth or a GeoJSON file?
column3: Lists → Places → “⤒ Import coordinates (KML, GeoJSON)”, or Settings → Import → “📍 Place coordinates”. Each point in the file (KML, KMZ or GeoJSON) is matched with a place in your database by its name, and the department settles namesakes. Line by line, you tick: add the coordinates to a place that has none, replace those of a place (unticked at first), choose between several places with the same name, or create the place. The KML and GeoJSON files exported by the app read back without loss. “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before.

column2: How do I open my genealogy in Obsidian (linked Markdown notes)?
column3: Settings → Export → “⤓ To other software and sites” → “🗒 For Obsidian”: a .zip file to unzip, then “Open folder as vault” in Obsidian. One note per person (identity, events, sources, notes) and one per place, linked by [[…]] links to the parents, children, spouses and places; the “Genealogy” note lists them all. You choose the whole database, your Sosa ancestors or a branch. Living people and confidential records stay hidden (“Living person”) or removed.

column2: How do I see my family network in Gephi, yEd or Graphviz?
column3: Settings → Export → “🕸 Network (GraphML)” for Gephi and yEd, or “🕸 Network (Graphviz)” for a .dot file (dot -Tsvg reseau.dot -o reseau.svg turns it into a drawing). Each person is a point with their name, sex, years, generation and Sosa number; each parent-child link and each couple is a line. Tick “one point per family” to put the couple between the parents and the children. Same privacy rules as the other exports.

column2: How do I send my DNA segments to DNA Painter, or import DNA Painter, Genetic Affairs and LivingDNA?
column3: “🧬 DNA” tab → 🧩 Chromosomes → “⤓ Export for DNA Painter”: a CSV file (the format of FamilyTreeDNA’s chromosome browser, which DNA Painter reads in “Paint a new match”). To import: “⤒ Import (CSV)” also recognises the export of a DNA Painter profile (segments, side, group, colour), Genetic Affairs’ AutoCluster and AutoTree files (each cluster becomes a group, the grid gives the shared matches, AutoTree gives the common ancestor) and LivingDNA’s list of matches. A raw DNA file is never imported.

column2: How do I import my photos from Google Photos or Apple Photos with their date and place?
column3: Lists → Media and documents → “⤒ Import photos”. Google Photos: the .zip archive from Google Takeout (1 GB at most; beyond that, unzip it and choose the photos with their .json files). Apple Photos: File → Export, with “Title, Keywords, and Caption” and “Location Information” (or with the .xmp files). The app takes over the date the photo was taken, the description, keywords and albums (as labels) and the GPS position. Places and named people are only suggested: tick “Link” for each one after checking. Everything is read on your computer, nothing is sent to the Internet. HEIC photos are left aside (export them as JPEG). “↶ Undo” removes everything that has just come in.

column2: Which DNA files can I import?
column3: “🧬 DNA” tab → Matches (or Chromosomes) → “⤒ Import (CSV)”: the lists of matches and segments exported by Ancestry (with DNAGedcom), MyHeritage, 23andMe, FamilyTreeDNA and GEDmatch. The company and the columns (cM, segments, longest segment, relationship, side, common ancestors, link to the profile or tree…) are recognised automatically; you can correct them in “Recognised columns”. “↶ Undo” right after puts everything back as before. A raw DNA file (your SNPs, the “raw data” file) is always refused: out of caution for your privacy and your family’s, and because in France a genetic test outside a medical or research setting is forbidden.

column2: How do I import a file (GEDCOM, CSV table, setting, list…)?
column3: All the “⤒ Import…” buttons open the same 3-step window: 1. drag the file (or paste it, or choose it); 2. you see what will come in (“12 people”, “34 rows”, the name of the setting…); 3. “⤒ Import”. When possible, the message that follows offers “↶ Undo”.

column2: Can the tab menu go at the bottom, or the column on the right?
column3: Yes: Settings → Appearance → “Tab menu” (top or bottom) and “Side column” (left or right), then Save.

column2: What do the colours of the badges (In progress, Done, Sosa…) mean?
column3: Everywhere in the app, the same colour means the same thing: blue = in progress, green = done or certain, yellow = to check, red = problem, grey = closed or archived, black = death. The Sosa number is always solid blue, on the record as in the picker. The record’s colours can still be set in Settings → Appearance → “Badge colours”.

column2: Why does the date show “today at 10:22” or “Tuesday”?
column3: The dates when something was created or edited are all written the same way: “today at…”, “yesterday at…”, the day of the week if it was less than 7 days ago, then “17 Oct 2026”. Hover over it to see the full date. The dates of your genealogy (births, records…) do not change.

column2: Something is missing in a window: where is the error?
column3: Just under the field to correct: it has a red frame, with the sentence that says what to do (“Give the widget a title.”), and the cursor is already there. If there are several things to correct, the window says so at the top (“2 things to fix before saving”). The window stays open: nothing you wrote is lost, and the red goes away as soon as you correct it. The message at the bottom left is now only used when saving itself fails.

column2: Why do all the windows have the same size and the same bottom?
column3: There are only 4 sizes: small for a question or a choice, medium for a form, large when there are two columns or a preview, very large for galleries of images and templates; editors (drawing, page layout, editing…) take the whole screen. The bottom of the window always stays visible when you scroll: “Delete” on the left, “Cancel” then the main button on the right; a window that only shows something has “Close”.

column2: Why do the buttons say “Create the book”, “Link” or “↺ Reset to default”?
column3: Everywhere, the same action has the same word and the same symbol. “Create the …” makes something new, “Save” keeps something that exists, “Add” puts one thing into another, “🔗 Link” attaches two records, “↺ Reset to default” returns to the starting settings, and a window that only shows something has “Close” alone. The symbols: ⤒ import, ⤓ export or download, 💾 save, 🖨 print, ✎ edit, 🗑 delete, ↗ open, ⚙️ settings, 🔍 search, ＋ add or new, 📋 copy, ⧉ duplicate, ⭐ favourite, 📁 file, × close.

column2: A block or a list is empty: how do I start?
column3: When there is nothing, the app always says so the same way: a large box for an empty page or list, a small line in a block (“📚 No sources”). Next to it, the button to start (“＋ Add…”) does the same thing as the usual button.

column2: How do I add a child, a parent or a spouse?
column3: Open the record, then in the Parents, Spouses or Children blocks click “＋”. You can choose a person who already exists or create a new one.

column2: How do I show a block (Departures, WWI soldier, Resistance member…) on a record?
column3: Record → Identity (pencil) → “Blocks to show on the record”: tick the block. To have it on all records: Settings → Appearance → “Blocks shown on request”.

column2: How do I create my own dashboard widget?
column3: Settings → Widget editor (or “＋ Create a widget” at the bottom of the dashboard column) → “＋ New widget”. Start from scratch (figures, list, chart, statistic, app screen, text, shortcuts), from any element of the app (a list, a diagram, a statistic, a record, the map, a tool), from an app widget (an editable copy, or the same widget dressed with your title, icon and colour), from one of your widgets or from an example. The preview updates while you adjust it. It then appears in the left column of the dashboard; “Share” turns it into a file for someone close to you.

column2: How do I arrange the dashboard into pages and groups?
column3: Dashboard → “Reorder the widgets”. “＋ New page” adds a page (List, Cards, Search…): its buttons appear at the top, under the title; tick the one that opens by default, and “Arrange its widgets” to organise it (widgets added from the left column go onto the page shown). “＋ Group” creates a frame with a title that gathers the widgets that follow it; ▶ makes it a sub-group, with as many levels as you like. The ▾ button to the left of the frame folds or opens the group.

column2: How do I move a row with the mouse?
column3: Wherever there are ↑ ↓ arrows, the ⠿ (or ↕) handle in front of the row can be dragged to the place you want.

column2: How do I create my own block?
column3: Settings → Block editor → “＋ New block”. Start from a template, an app block (Departures, WWI soldier, Resistance member, Grave…) or one of your blocks, add or remove fields by clicking the buttons, then save. It then appears in Identity → “Blocks to show on the record”. The “📊 Chart” field places a chart fully set up in the Chart editor (“New chart…”, then back to the block); with the criterion “Relative to the person on the record”, it counts their ancestors, descendants, family… The “🧱 Widget” field places one of your widgets (figures, list, chart…) or an app screen (the person’s record, a list, a diagram…).

column2: How do I add a label?
column3: In almost every form, the “🏷️ Labels” line: click “＋”, type the beginning of the name or create a new label. The list of all labels is in Lists → Labels.

column2: How do I spot a generation mistake (a father confused with his son of the same name)?
column3: Settings → ✅ Database check (🎂 Ages badge): besides ages at marriage and parents who are too young or too old, a set of siblings spread over two generations, a Sosa ancestor too young or too old for their place in the line, a death before birth or a marriage after death.

column2: How do I protect a record against changes?
column3: The padlock at the top of the record locks it: nothing can be changed there any more, not even by working together.

column2: Who is the root person (de cujus), and why do they have Sosa number 1?
column3: The root person (de cujus) is the starting person of the tree: they are Sosa number 1, their father 2, their mother 3, and so on. Go menu → “Root person” (⌘⇧H or Ctrl+Shift+H) opens their record. To change: Settings → Appearance → Sosa numbering, look for the person then “Recalculate”; the choice is saved in the database, so it follows the backup and another computer.
